question.worked_solution:
Given an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ we have

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}.
$$

First, we find $|A|$ using a Laplace expansion across the $2$nd row:

$$
\begin{aligned}|A| & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & -4 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ -3 & 5 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}|+3(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}|+2(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-12+20)+3(24-12)-2(20-6) \\  & =8+36-28 \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}=\frac{1}{16}.
$$
